Location: [Insert Location]
Customer: Lance
## Overview
The consultation centers on configuring the Virtual Contact Assistant (VCA), named “Kaylee,” for Lance’s automotive dealerships (Porsche, Audi, BMW). Initial rollout starts with Porsche (ID: 21013). The goals are to align Kaylee’s behavior with the current Podium AI—setting appointments and engaging customers without confusion—while refining persona (human vs. virtual), pricing disclosure, texting hours, tone, and re-engagement logic. Key focus areas include preventing conversation restarts caused by frequent “Notify Assistant” steps, streamlining migrated instructions from Podium to fit platform constraints, and tailoring brand-specific rules (e.g., Porsche MSRP vs. Audi Internet Price). Final advanced options, process customizations, and suppression rules will be completed with Project Manager Gage, with activation planned in about five days.
## Background
Lance manages configurations for Porsche, Audi, and BMW dealerships and is transitioning from Podium to Kaylee. The initial configuration targets Harish Porsche, with plans to replicate optimized settings across Audi and BMW. The team also uses Predictive Insights; Gen AI availability varies by store (Harish Porsche lacks Gen AI). The meeting is a follow-up to review and refine settings, including advanced options and special instructions migrated from Podium, before a final session with Gage and full rollout next week.
## Pain Points
- Conversation resets: Each “Notify Assistant” step relaunches a fresh conversation, causing loss of context and repetitive customer experiences. Daily and periodic notifications (days 1–6, 9, 11, 15, 22) frequently re-start threads. Auto-pause is overridden by subsequent notifications unless suppression is applied.
- Persona and operational rules: Uncertainty about presenting Kaylee as human vs. virtual assistant affects customer perception, error handling, and stakeholder alignment across brands.
- After-hours messaging compliance: Desire for 24/7 responsiveness conflicts with unknown state-specific regulations, creating legal risk for late-night automated texts.
- Instruction bloat and character limits: Migrated Podium content includes redundant details (address, hours, tone) already covered by system settings. The 1500-character limit constrains inclusion of more critical rules, risking inefficiency and inconsistency.
- Service inquiry handling: Prior tools were bogged down by service questions; Lance wants to ensure Kaylee avoids service topics or routes appropriately.
- Cross-store configuration clarity: Some settings can be copied; others (pricing permissions, brand-specific custom instructions) must be set individually. Gen AI capability inconsistencies complicate rollout.
## Expectations
- Align Kaylee’s behavior with Podium: actively manage interactions, set general appointments for test drives/appraisals without committing to specific vehicle availability, and stay engaged unless manually paused by sales.
- Brand-specific pricing rules: Porsche to disclose MSRP; Audi to disclose Internet Price with discounts highlighted.
- Controlled communication parameters: Configure texting hours and tone (“friendly,” greet by name), ensure compliance with state regulations, and define re-engagement logic (currently set for ninety days of inactivity).
- Streamlined instruction set: Remove redundant information to free space for critical, brand-specific rules (e.g., out-of-state buyers, EV/hybrid specifics).
- Process ownership: PM Gage to copy/create AI-integrated internet sales flows and finalize advanced options, suppressions, and re-engagement rules across all stores before go-live.
## Other Information Summary
- Free training: VCA training Tuesdays/Thursdays via eAcademy; Predictive Insights & Gen AI training Monday–Friday.
- Kaylee will handle internet sales leads, after-hours sales, showroom follow-ups, appointment reminders, and follow-ups for missed/canceled appointments.
- Salespeople labeled “client advisors”; customers “clients.”
- Manual “Pause Assistant” acts as a catch-all to stop all AI communications until un-paused.
- Consultant cannot modify pricing permissions or differentiator parts; Lance must configure these per store.
- Porsche currently lacks Gen AI; Audi/BMW have varied histories with the feature.
## To-Do List
- [ ] Coordinate with PM Gage to review and finalize VCA advanced options, process customizations, and suppression rules; build “flow with VA” for all stores.
- [ ] Implement suppression rules to prevent re-notifications after human contact; adjust notification cadence to reduce conversation restarts.
- [ ] Decide on persona (human vs. virtual) after consulting store managers; consider neutral/hybrid introduction scripts.
- [ ] Verify state regulations for after-hours automated texting; set compliant texting windows (e.g., no scheduling past 6 PM if desired).
- [ ] Streamline special instructions by removing redundant details; create brand-specific modules for Porsche, Audi, BMW within character limits.
- [ ] Double-check financing application URLs for all locations.
- [ ] Confirm and set pricing permissions for Audi and BMW; replicate general settings from Porsche to Audi and BMW.
- [ ] Inform staff about available VCA and Predictive Insights/Gen AI training; schedule finalization meeting with Gage; send recap email.
## AI Suggestions
1. Implement aggressive suppression rules: Suppress “Notify Assistant” steps for 2–3 days following any logged human interaction to prevent redundant fresh starts; ensure auto-pause isn’t overridden by scheduled notifications.
2. Consolidate AI notification cadence: Reduce daily notifications to fewer, spaced-out steps (e.g., Day 1, Day 3, Day 7) to limit restart risk and give sales time to engage.
3. Establish a human takeover workflow: Train sales to use “Pause Assistant” immediately during substantive conversations (financing, trade-ins) to avoid AI interference until re-engagement is desired.
4. Use task-based triggers: Where possible, trigger AI re-engagement based on customer inactivity or task completion rather than fixed time intervals for more context-relevant outreach.
5. Phased persona rollout: Start with “Virtual Assistant” persona across all stores for 30–60 days; review performance, then revisit human persona as needed.
6. Create a best-practices one-pager: Summarize pros/cons of human vs. virtual personas with examples; equip managers to decide confidently.
7. Adopt a neutral introduction: “I’m Kaylee, here to assist you at [Dealership Name]” and disclose AI nature only if asked or when conversations exceed scope.
8. Build a master template of refined instructions: Remove system-defined variables and redundancies; use modular blocks (General Rules, EV/Hybrid, Out-of-State Buyers) to ease brand-specific customization.
9. Conduct a configuration audit with Gage: Review screens to clarify which fields are redundant and which require per-store settings; align on copying vs. customizing.

recordings.summary_md:
## VCA staff training (VinSolutions) — Michael Pratt

Tue Sep 15 lecture for sales + managers on **Virtual Contact Assistant** (“Vanessa”).

**What it is:** Behind-the-scenes AI that engages customers, books appointments, gathers info. When she can’t handle a request (discount, trade, credit, etc.), she creates a **needs-help task** for the salesperson.

**Sales play:**
- Live on the task page; find the Vanessa banner
- Open customer profile → review Vanessa thread (don’t rely on generic “needs help” alone)
- Contact the customer, then **Complete** the task — never **Dismiss** (reads as ignored)
- Sentiment colors are keyword-ish; always read the thread
- Pause 1–30 days when customer asks no AI / vacation / negative thread; managers resume from profile or pause list

**Managers:** Live view of VA emails/texts; Insight Virtual Assistant Dashboard; Settings → Dealer Settings → Virtual Assistant Settings (pause list).

**Config notes from room:** VA often has its own text line vs dealership SMS (confirmed pattern on Harris Porsche in-session). Appointments follow store hours.

**Dest:** dealers (BH group VCA path).  
**Disposition:** park — training reference for Sep 21 cutover; no new build WO.

recordings.summary_md:
## Software factory full pass — Isolate → Build → Prove → Ship

Continuation of Schmidt factory talk. Four-step conveyor for multi-agent feature work.

### Steps
1. **Isolate / Team** — worktrees/branches so ~50 agents can ship parallel features without overwriting (agents.md + new-feature skill)
2. **Build** — code-structure skill forces service-layer architecture (less slop, human/agent-readable)
3. **Prove** — evidence-driven testing (before/after video) + before/after screenshots in PRs; non-visual = measured numbers; auto-loop back to Build if proof fails
4. **Ship** — external review agent (Greptile/CodeRabbit/Macroscope) confidence score; loop until 5/5 then human merge

### Factory analogy
Order station → assembly line → QC → package/deploy. Software factory = markdown workflows, not a vendor product.

### Action in source
- Rename Isolate → Team (speaker)
- Coop: park as architecture reference for Acquire/agent factory discipline

## Meeting Notes
### Recall Campaign Strategy for Non-DMS Customers
- Proposal: Contact all customers not in the DMS to bring their cars in for recalls.
- Concern: Older models (e.g., VANOS, water pump) pose higher breakage risk during repairs.
- Parameters discussed: Set a hard stop by model year to mitigate risk.
- Decision: Limit campaign to vehicles from model year 2015 and newer.
- Outreach channels: Email, mail, text, and voice messages targeting ~2,700 nearby BMW owners.
- Service scope: Include appointment scheduling, functioning as a BDC for recall-related services.
### Website Service Coupon Discussion
- Goal: Implement a 10% off service coupon on the company website to attract customers.
- Max discount debated: $150 or $200 initially; prior Epsilon email blasts used $100 max.
- Competitor review: Brian Harris’s site appears to offer 10% with no stated maximum, posing potential risk.
- Focus: Define clear exclusions for the offer.
- Conclusion: Add a 10% off service coupon with a $100 maximum discount; exclusions include value service, tires, and glass.
## Next Arrangements
- [ ] Talk to Caleb about setting parameters for the recall campaign, specifically enforcing a hard stop for cars older than the 2015 model year.
- [ ] Check with Michael to confirm whether the competitor’s (Brian Harris) coupon has a maximum discount.
- [ ] Add the 10% off service coupon to the website with a $100 maximum discount, excluding value service, tires, and glass.

recordings.name: 09-09 Reasoning-Note: Action Plan for Automotive Service Revenue Turnaround Amid Leadership Scrutiny
recordings.work_order: Tomorrow with Rick: CP service turnaround + April Bower knowledge-share; Open Roads COO (Scott Cusick) audit prep
recordings.summary_md:
![PLAUD NOTE](permanent/1440a4fbcf984caa9625e6345e38a215/mem_g5kZLYofe1/summary_poster/card_20260909135233-v2@5d98d896f6fb3033116fc1_20260909135359_c75d7407.png)

## Core Synopsis
The business is under dual pressure: service revenue is missing daily targets and leadership scrutiny is about to intensify. Operationally, stores are meeting or exceeding some front-end retail metrics, but customer-pay service throughput and dollar volume are underperforming despite high labor costs and nine techs on the floor. Politically, Open Roads hired a seasoned COO (ex-Lithia M&A) who will run a forensic review, while ownership has discovered absentee executive leadership, heightening the risk of top-down intervention. Evidence points to a capacity-and-culture problem in Service: an underperforming, change-resistant shop foreman, talent scarcity in Jackson, and insufficient sales/service advisor horsepower are constraining RO count and average dollars per RO. Advisory support is weak; field reps flag gaps but provide “sell more parts” guidance without process repairs. Meanwhile, the team is rationalizing spend (cut Cars.com and Automotive Mastermind), experimenting with Podium and AI call-routing to avoid adding headcount, and planning an internal newsletter to boost engagement. We are accountable for reversing service underperformance before the COO’s audit converts soft misses (−$81k YTD bonuses) into hard structural mandates; we commit to a focused reset on technician productivity, advisor effectiveness, and leadership accountability in the shop.

## Service Revenue Turnaround: From Fragmented Effort to Focused System
- The Constraints Driving the Shortfall (Diagnostic Deep-Dive)
  - Phenomenon: Customer-pay workshop sales must hit ~$7.5k/day net but are missing, despite nine technicians.
  - Mechanism: Low technician productivity and/or under-optimized dispatch; inadequate service advisor selling (ARO, MPIs, menuing); leadership blockage from a 30-year shop foreman resisting new process; recruiting constraints in Jackson shrink the quality talent pool.
  - Root Causes:
    - Process: Inconsistent RO build depth (inspections, fluid exchanges, maintenance menus) and weak parts/service coordination for same-day approvals.
    - People: Advisor counts and closing skills are insufficient to lift CP ARO; shop foreman undercuts change adoption; billable hours per tech likely below target due to dispatch/load leveling gaps and comeback/hold times.
    - Tools: Phone triage and routing improved with Podium AI pilot, but service scheduling, MPI photo/video usage, and follow-up may lack rigor; vendor “advice” is informational, not operational.
- The Near-Term Audit Reality (Challenge-Response)
  - Status Quo: YTD missed bonuses of ~$81k; other stores (e.g., “battle lines” at 105%) are outperforming.
  - Imminent Gap: New COO Scott Cusick will drill into CP revenue, labor efficiency, ARO, effective labor rate (ELR), parts-to-labor ratios, and advisor close rates.
  - Response: Preempt the audit by installing a visible playbook—daily RO targets by advisor, hours per RO goals by tech, foreman accountability, and same-day upsell cadence—so the narrative shifts from excuses to measurable recovery.
- Leadership and Culture Reset in the Shop (Dialectical Analysis)
  - Thesis: Long-tenured foreman stability provides tribal knowledge.
  - Antithesis: “We’ve always done it this way” blocks throughput, modern MPI-driven selling, and dispatch optimization.
  - Synthesis: Retain tribal knowledge but remove the veto power—reassign or replace the foreman role if KPIs slip; empower a lead willing to run load balancing, enforce MPIs, and coach techs on billed hours targets.
- Capacity and Mix: Advisors, Techs, and the Phone Front Door (Structural Assembly)
  - Technicians: Nine techs require strong dispatching and steady feeder work. Without advisor-driven approvals, tech idle time rises and CP falls.
  - Service Advisors: Add or upskill to lift ARO via rigorous MPIs, photo/video transparency, menu presentations, and same-day decisioning scripts.
  - Phone and Scheduling: Podium AI call-routing trial is a cost-efficient hedge; ROI depends on reducing abandoned calls, accelerating appointment setting, and routing to the right advisor without extra headcount.
- Vendor and Spend Rationalization (Trade-Offs with Teeth)
  - Cuts: Cars.com and Automotive Mastermind removed; ad spend normalized to ~$25k after credits; Podium added for service communications and AI phone support.
  - Trade-off: Lower third-party lead spend demands higher conversion of in-house traffic; service must offset with process-driven ARO and ELR gains.
- Internal Communication and Morale Levers
  - Newsletter/Magazine: Use “Employee of the Month” and role spotlights (e.g., new parts manager Shelley) to reinforce desired behaviors and retention amid market hiring challenges.

## Action Items

**@Service Manager (Jackson)**
- [ ] Pull last 60 days of service KPIs: CP RO count, CP ARO, hours per RO, ELR, tech efficiency/utilization, advisor close rates, parts-to-labor ratio, comeback rate - [TBD]
- [ ] Implement daily CP revenue targets per advisor and hours targets per tech; publish a scoreboard at open/close of day - [TBD]
- [ ] Enforce 100% MPI with photo/video and a standard menu presentation on every RO; audit 10 ROs/day for compliance - [TBD]
- [ ] Reassign or place the shop foreman on a 30-day performance plan tied to tech billed hours/utilization and MPI compliance; prepare successor plan - [TBD]

**@Parts Manager (Shelley)**
- [ ] Set same-day parts SLAs for common maintenance/repair menus (stock levels, bin locations, response times); report fill rate and turnaround weekly - [TBD]

**@Lance**
- [ ] Schedule a 30-minute knowledge-share with April Bower (Brian Harris) on advisor workflows, dispatch discipline, and ARO lifts; document 5 adoptable practices - [TBD]
- [ ] Define Podium AI success criteria (call answer rate, time-to-appointment, transfer accuracy); review 30/60/90-day ROI to decide continue vs. hire - [TBD]

**@Owner/GM (Local Store Lead)**
- [ ] Prepare a pre-audit brief for COO Scott Cusick: baseline service KPIs, 90-day turnaround plan, weekly cadence, and named owners - [TBD]

recordings.summary_md:
Date & Time: 2026-09-08 13:04:01
Location: [Insert Location]
Customer: Lance
Overview
The consultation covers configuring and rolling out a Virtual Conversation/Contact Assistant (VCA GenAI) to replace Podium across three dealerships: Brian Harris BMW, Audi Baton Rouge, and Harris Porsche. Objectives include replicating and enhancing Podium’s nuanced, campaign-specific messaging for varied lead types (e.g., manufacturer lease maturity/NCI vs. standard web leads), enabling natural initial SMS via the new Established Business Relationship (EBR) setting, and implementing role-based guardrails, tone/persona customization, and dealership differentiators. The VCA will automate follow-ups, appointment setting, trade-in info gathering, vehicle interest confirmation, and support Internet and showroom processes, with clear sequencing and suppressions to avoid overlap. A controlled rollout is targeted before the “go dark” date on September 21, followed by monitoring and iterative optimization, including portfolio-style engagement for NCI lease leads.
Background
- Lance, a seasoned consultant supporting the three dealerships, seeks full adoption and a seamless transition by September 21.
- All stores currently use Podium; the integrated VCA GenAI will replace it. BMW has Predictive Insights (underused), and all three stores have access to the Insights VCA dashboard (attempted/actual contacts, appointments, active conversations).
- Training is scheduled for next week, with a 5–7 day buffer before go-live; the system will run the last eight to nine days of September with early October review.
- Processes include timing (e.g., 25 minutes within business hours after a 12-hour window), suppressions to prevent overlap with salesperson activity, and generic tasks to notify reps.
- Audi NCI-like manufacturer leads arrive as web leads with distinct source codes; BMW receives explicit NCI (e.g., 270-day lease portfolio leads).
- The assistant has been renamed to “Chloe,” with planned profile updates for consistency.
Pain Points
- Replicating Podium’s nuanced, lead-type-specific messaging: BMW FS/NCI vs. Audi web leads require distinct scripts and rules to avoid generic outreach and awkward first messages.
- Initial opt-in friction: Default VCA opt-in as the first SMS feels unnatural; EBR should enable immediate, relevant conversation for inquiry-based leads.
- Guardrails and conversation policies: No predefined rules for sensitive topics (e.g., pricing), risking misaligned conversations and compliance issues without explicit hand-offs to sales.
- Reporting access and visibility: Permission settings risk oversharing; managers need dashboard access while limiting reps’ visibility to all customers.
- Process design complexity: Timing, suppressions, and task sequencing must be tuned to avoid misfires, duplication, and clutter.
- NCI strategy uncertainty: Limited precedent for VCA engaging manufacturer lease maturity leads; differences in OEM feeds complicate routing and tone.
- Duplicate after-hours messaging: Podium and VCA both sending messages created confusion; after-hours VCA was disabled across stores as a temporary fix.
- Adoption and training risk: Managers and reps need clear guidance on pause lists, inbox/notes visibility, sentiment interpretation, and escalation to ensure consistent use.
Expectations
- Fully replicate and surpass Podium’s capabilities by September 21, including tailored flows for distinct lead types and natural initial SMS via EBR.
- Configure tone/persona, dealership differentiators, and explicit guardrails (e.g., pricing escalation to sales) prior to go-live; measure appointments, engagement quality, and reduced escalations.
- Establish reporting permissions so managers access dashboards while restricting rep overexposure; verify Insights favorites and data accuracy.
- Enable and tune Internet and showroom follow-up processes with minute-based offsets, suppressions, and clear task wording; copy processes to accelerate setup.
- Pilot NCI engagement with portfolio-manager voice (pre-inspection, supportive messaging) for BMW 270-day lease leads and Audi source-coded leads; iterate based on early results.
- Conduct role-based training, reinforce adoption, and monitor pause lists and sentiment 2–3 times weekly; schedule pre–September 21 final check and early October review.
Other Information Summary
- VCA adapts to preferred channels (text/email) and switches mid-conversation; reps can pause VCA, and logs are visible in inbox and notes/history.
- Negative sentiment may be productive (e.g., scheduling conflicts) and should be interpreted carefully.
- Customer prefers keeping “disengage virtual assistant when a human contacts the customer” disabled so VCA can re-engage if a salesperson lapses.
- Upcoming Acquisition feature aligns with Audi’s KBB ICO vehicle acquisition leads.
- Lance functions as first-line support across stores and is comfortable with technical configuration.
To-Do List
- Lance: Enable EBR in SMS settings for all stores to ensure natural initial conversations.
- Lance: Review Podium campaigns and lead handling rules to prepare VCA replication; compile dealership differentiators and finalize tone/persona and pricing guardrails (within 5–7 days post-training).
- Lance: Update VCA user profile to “Chloe” (name, email) for consistent communications.
- Consultant: Provide configuration guidance for lead-type-specific conversational flows (BMW FS/NCI vs. standard web leads); review and enable Internet/showroom processes with tuned timing/suppressions and task wording.
- Admin: Set reporting permissions (enable “CRM reports and my dashboards” for managers; restrict reps); favorite the VCA dashboard and verify metrics.
- Team: Design and launch NCI pilot (map Audi source codes; draft portfolio-manager scripts for BMW 270-day cadence); iterate post-launch.
- Training team: Prepare role-based materials (pause list cadence, inbox/notes use, sentiment handling) ahead of next week’s sessions.
- Managers/Lance: Establish monitoring cadence (pause list 2–3x weekly; spot-check negative sentiment); document escalation rules and hand-off scripts (e.g., pricing inquiries).
- Scheduling: Final review before September 21; go-live for last eight to nine days of September; follow-up review in early October and additional check-ins over the first four to five weeks.
AI Suggestions
- Lead Source-Based Workflow Mapping: Workshop every lead source and communication path, then configure VCA triggers and scripts to preserve “little tweaks.”
- Phased Rollout/Pilot: Validate complex lead types (manufacturer/NCI) at one store (e.g., Audi or BMW) before full cutover on the 21st.
- Configuration Playbook: Create a modular playbook for guardrails, tone, lead-type scripts, and escalation triggers to enable ongoing tweaks.
- Dynamic AI Responses: Train GenAI to recognize lease maturity context and adjust tone/questions beyond rigid rules.
- Guardrail Implementation: Add rules-based suppressions and keyword triggers (price/discount/out-the-door) to auto-escalate and pause VCA; use templated hand-off scripts.
- Controlled A/B Tests: Trial guardrail variations on a subset of Internet leads; measure appointments, escalation rates, and conversation quality.
- After-Hours Strategy: Migrate fully from Podium to VCA to eliminate duplicates; if both must remain, consider time-sharing or API-based handoff; clarify role-based specialization to avoid overlap.

recordings.name: Planning: Dealership Website Optimization and VCA Integration Rollout
recordings.work_order: VCA trainings Sep 14–16 2pm CT; cutover Sep 21 vs Podium. Gray Media land on model research page (email Macy). Review Podium campaigns for Ven/VCA replication.
recordings.summary_md:
![PLAUD NOTE](permanent/1440a4fbcf984caa9625e6345e38a215/mem_g5kZLYofe1/summary_poster/card_20260908191753-v2@dfe3c24e5bab9cf658b145_20260908191856_46707fb5.png)

Lance and Speaker 1 reviewed website performance metrics to address short session durations from top-funnel traffic channels. They decided to redirect promotional traffic to a specialized model research page and reviewed updated dashboard reporting. Lance also coordinated with Michael from Event Solutions to schedule Virtual Contact (VCA) training sessions for staff at three dealership locations, timing the transition to align with their existing software contract termination.

## Website Traffic and Landing Page Optimization

- **Session Duration Metrics**: Speaker 1 noted that the average session duration across the website was only 23 seconds. Lance stated his target for average user engagement is over three minutes, though two to three minutes is a typical benchmark. To increase session duration, the team has discussed launching a newsletter on the site and adding more vehicle photos.
- **Traffic Source Analysis**: The 23-second average session duration was traced to traffic coming from Gray Media campaigns. Lance explained that Gray Media runs high-funnel awareness campaigns similar to brand-level campaigns run by Audi. This type of traffic naturally produces higher bounce rates and shorter session durations than low-funnel sources like Google Ads or retargeting campaigns, which target shoppers who are already looking for specific lease rates or vehicles.
- **Landing Page Strategy**: To capture high-funnel traffic more effectively, Lance proposed changing the destination link. Instead of directing Gray Media traffic to the generic homepage, they will direct users to a long model research page that Lance previously built. This page presents multiple model options and brand entry points, which should help keep uncommitted shoppers on the site longer.
- **Traffic Volumes**: Direct traffic reached 20,400 visits for the period from August 9 to September 8, 2026, matching similar trends from the previous month. Organic search continues to drive the bulk of the dealership's business, bringing in over 10,000 visits.
- **Dashboard Reporting Integration**: The traffic data is pulled directly from Google Analytics 4 (GA4). Lance upgraded the GM weekly dashboard to show granular metrics for each source and medium. The updated dashboard breaks down visits, unique visitors, average session duration, and mobile actions like phone taps. Lance is currently working to filter out programmatic traffic sources that route through intermediate platforms like FlashTalking.

## Virtual Contact Integration and Training

- **System Rollout and Contract Alignment**: Lance is coordinating the Virtual Contact (VCA) setup across three locations: Harris Porsche, Audi Baton Rouge, and Brian Harris BMW. Lance worked with Jeff Elliman to schedule the technical transition for September 21, 2026. This date matches the end of their contract with Podium, preventing the dealerships from being double-billed for both platforms.
- **Training Session Coordination**: Lance and Michael from Event Solutions agreed to schedule three separate one-hour training sessions on consecutive weekdays:
  - **Dates**: Monday, September 14, Tuesday, September 15, and Wednesday, September 16, 2026.
  - **Time**: All sessions are scheduled for 2:00 PM Central (3:00 PM Eastern). This afternoon slot avoids early morning or late afternoon sales rushes.
  - **Format**: Each session is dedicated to one of the three stores, but the schedule will be shared across all locations. Staff members who cannot attend their store's assigned day due to scheduling conflicts or days off may join one of the alternate sessions. Lance plans to connect his laptop in the conference rooms to attend and facilitate all three sessions.
- **Setup and Integration Workflow**: Lance scheduled a meeting with an internal team member at 1:00 PM on September 8, 2026, to begin initial VCA configurations. Lance plans to review their active Podium campaigns to ensure their historical data and specialized setups are ready for integration into Ven. 
- **Opt-In Messaging Compliance**: Lance and Michael discussed message compliance workflows. Podium did not require prior customer opt-in and instead included a "reply STOP to opt out" footer in text messages. Ven's default workflow involves sending an initial automated opt-in request text, which can feel unnatural to customers. Lance noted that Ven allows staff to manually check the opt-in box within the workflow, bypassing the automated opt-in text for established leads.

## Tangent: Disc Golf Discussion

The mid-section of the recording contains an extended segment featuring participants discussing disc golf gameplay, course design at Red Apple Farm, and individual disc selection for their MVP disc bags.

## Action Items

**@Lance**
- [ ] Email Macy to discuss redirecting Gray Media traffic from the homepage to the model research page
- [ ] Review active Podium campaigns to prepare for Ven integration, Deadline: 2026-09-08
- [ ] Connect to the conference rooms and attend the three VCA training sessions to support dealership staff, Deadline: 2026-09-16

**@Michael (Event Solutions)**
- [ ] Conduct the three scheduled VCA training sessions for the dealerships on September 14, 15, and 16, 2026, at 2:00 PM Central, Deadline: 2026-09-16

## Overview
The consultation focused on transitioning Brian Harris BMW from their current marketing automation platform (AMP) to Fullpath’s Audience Activation and Customer Data Platform (CDP). The customer, Lance, is also moving off Podium and needs to replace its chat and review functionalities. The primary pain points are the inefficiency of the current AMP system generating unqualified leads, limited data breadth for precise targeting, underutilization of service campaigns, and the manual effort required to move slow inventory.
The vendor presented how Fullpath’s Audience Activation, powered by an enriched CDP, would use broader data (including offsite shopping behavior from AutoTrader/KBB, Equifax data, etc.) to drive omni-channel campaigns, improve targeting, and deliver real-time shopper insights. The discussion also covered Fullpath's dynamic chat tool and its ability to re-engage past customers ("defectors") for an associated Audi dealership. Desired outcomes include a more efficient, integrated system that qualifies leads before creating tasks, improves ROI, enables more precise targeting, enhances service/recall engagement, accelerates inventory movement, and provides access to unified analytics.
## Background
- **Customer Context**: Brian Harris BMW is currently using an older version of AMP, managed by Lance, who keeps about thirty default campaigns live with 2–4 ad hoc monthly updates (APR/lease offers, slow-moving inventory). The dealership is also ceasing its use of Podium for review invites, AI BDC, and website chat.
- **Performance**: The current AMP has shown strong ROI, generating “twenty sales for eighty-four grand” and “three hundred and eighty-two repair orders for two hundred and ninety-eight thousand dollars” in the last 60 days.
- **Proposal**: Replace AMP with Fullpath Audience Activation at the same monthly cost ($1,900/month), with the CDP provided free for 60 days (then optional at $9.99/month). A new dynamic chat tool is also available for $900/month. The new platform leverages a CDP to integrate data from Cox products, CRM, DMS, inventory feeds, VAuto, websites, and ads, enriched with Equifax data for accurate contact/equity information.
- **Tools**: Fullpath offers omni-channel (email/SMS) outreach with FTC-compliant AI-generated content, a Virtual Customer Assistant (VCA), and the Omni analytics platform for insights into sales, marketing, and service performance.
- **Group Opportunity**: An associated Audi store is resistant to the old AMP but could be pitched the new Fullpath platform as a replacement for its Mastermind software to target defected customers.
## Pain Points
- **Inefficient Lead Generation & Wasted Time**: The primary pain point is that the current AMP creates tasks indiscriminately for any marketing interaction, overwhelming the sales team with low-quality follow-ups on non-qualified leads. This "bullshit" behavior wastes time, causes staff to manually "fish" for real opportunities, and leads to missed revenue.
- **Limited Targeting Precision & Data Breadth**: The current AMP setup relies on basic, static campaigns ("nothing fancy") running off internal data, lacking the broader, CDP-level insights from offsite shopper behavior. This limits personalization and the ability to engage shoppers dynamically across channels.
- **Disjointed Tools & Fragmented Reporting**: Lance is moving off Podium and needs an integrated replacement for its chat and review functions. He has also built custom dashboards because existing reporting tools are "brutal" and make it "really hard to see all that in one place," indicating a need for a unified analytics view.
- **Underutilization of Service & Recall Campaigns**: The store “doesn’t do a lot of service” campaign activation, leading to missed revenue and retention opportunities. Campaigns for tires, brakes, service page abandonment, and recalls are not fully leveraged.
- **Customer Defection at Sister Store**: The Audi dealership has a significant problem with customer defection due to slow product cycles. They need a tool to effectively run re-engagement campaigns targeting customers from up to six years ago, as their current tool (Mastermind) is insufficient.
- **Manual Management of Slow Inventory**: Lance gives "a little extra love" to slow-moving "problem child" inventory via ad hoc monthly updates. This is a manual process that lacks integrated behavioral signals to proactively identify and target high-intent shoppers for these specific VINs.
- **Lack of Rapid Lead Injection Capability**: The dealership lacks an agile process to inject high-propensity leads into the CRM on-demand to meet end-of-month sales targets.
## Expectations
- **Improve Lead Quality and Sales Efficiency**: The primary expectation is that Fullpath will intelligently qualify leads via its VCA, only creating tasks for genuine "hand raisers." Success will be measured by a reduction in wasted sales time and increased conversions from marketing efforts.
- **Achieve Better ROI with Broader Data**: Leverage the CDP-driven Audience Activation to outperform AMP on the same budget ($1,900/month). Success metrics include higher open rates (targeting 84%+), increased sales/service ROI, and faster movement of slow VINs. The CDP will be trialed for 60 days.
- **Consolidate Tools with an Integrated Platform**: Find a comprehensive, integrated replacement for Podium's services, specifically a more advanced chat tool that is BMW co-op eligible. Lance also expects robust, consolidated reporting and the ability to schedule automated data exports to feed his existing structures.
- **Expand Service and Recall Outreach**: Activate a robust set of OEM-compliant service campaigns (op codes, A/B service, page abandon, recall) to increase ROs beyond the current 382 per 60 days and drive service-to-sale conversions.
- **Win Over the Resistant Audi Dealership**: Successfully re-pitch the "drastically different" Fullpath platform to the Audi GM, demonstrating its ability to replace Mastermind and effectively target defected customers to win their business.
- **Enable Proactive Inventory Management & Month-End Lead Injection**: Use the CDP/Omni to identify slow VINs and target high-intent shoppers. Establish a "Data Ups" process to push high-AIM (≥8), high-credit (≥750) prospects into the CRM to meet month-end targets.

- **Pricing**: Audience Activation is $1,900/month. The contract is month-to-month. The CDP is free for the first 60 days, then $9.99/month. The new chat tool is $900/month and is BMW co-op eligible.

- **Data Enrichment & Scale**: The platform uses Equifax to enrich customer data (contact info, garage, equity). A Chicago store example cited 8 million data points processed in one week, identifying 192,000 unique shoppers.
- **Onboarding**: The transition to the new platform is estimated to take about one week. The vendor's team will handle the co-op submission process with BMW.

recordings.name: 09-02 Leveraging Five GitHub Repositories to Enhance AI Agent Workflows and Operational Efficiency
recordings.summary_md:
![PLAUD NOTE](permanent/1440a4fbcf984caa9625e6345e38a215/mem_g5kZLYofe1/summary_poster/card_20260902215140-v2@dbe2e846e6a3b3950ce372_20260902215237_496fc5bc.png)

## Core Synopsis
The session spotlights five GitHub repos as practical leverage for builders operating in the “agentic” era: an anti-AI-tone editor (Peter Skill), an agent-native CRM (TryComp AI), an agent-driven video editor (VideoUse), NVIDIA’s security scanner for skills (SkillSpecter), and a phone-control harness (PhoneHarness). The throughline is blunt: current AI-generated content erodes trust, manual CRMs decay without automation, content throughput throttles growth, the expanding ecosystem of agent “skills” carries nontrivial security risk, and mobile remains an under-automated surface. The presenter positions these repos as modular upgrades to credibility, revenue capture, content velocity, security posture, and device coverage; the evidence is specific workflows (e.g., “remove AI sanding,” agent-managed follow-ups, repeatable edit formats, pre-install scans, real-device mobile QA) and concrete setup steps (Bun/Docker pipelines, OAuth, UV tool installs, ADB/mirroring). We are committing to a hybrid workflow philosophy: human-originated ideas and constraints first, then agents for repeatable, tedious execution. The stakes are clear—builders who operationalize these patterns gain compounding edge in output and trust; those who “one-shot” content, let pipelines rot, skip security, or ignore mobile interfaces will leak opportunity and credibility.

## Operational System Upgrades: Five Repos, Five Leverage Points

### Eliminate “AI Slop” to Preserve Voice and Trust
- Problem: AI-written copy “smells” formulaic—polished but generic—reducing reader trust and engagement.
- Solution: Peter Skill acts as an editor that detects/removes AI-pattern artifacts while preserving the author’s voice.
- Workflow Principle: Human-first drafting (outline and real points) → skill-driven de-sanding pass; avoid AI one-shot generation that erases differentiation.
- Intended Outcome: Higher believability and response rates across tweets, landing pages, cold emails, launch posts, onboarding copy, and investor updates.

### Convert CRM from Filing Cabinet to Agent Workspace
- Reality: Traditional CRMs decay because humans won’t maintain them; warm opportunities die in stale notes.
- Repo: TryComp AI’s open-source agent-native CRM; the agent researches, enriches, schedules follow-ups, and updates notes to keep relationship graphs alive.
- Use Cases: Sponsorship pipelines, investor update follow-through, waitlist re-engagement, small SaaS customer success, agency lead tracking.
- Practical Start: Create a narrow pipeline (“Warm leads I can’t afford to forget”), ingest every signal of intent (reply, booked call, “circle back” dates), let the agent maintain the cadence.
- Setup Snapshot: Requires Bun and Docker; steps include git clone, bun install, docker compose up -d, db deploy/seed, bun run dev; runs on localhost:3000 (API: 3001); configure Google/Microsoft OAuth for sign-in/email/calendar.

### Codify Video Editing so Agents Can Execute at Scale
- Bottleneck: Content throughput is a growth constraint; creators repeat predictable edit patterns but keep them implicit.
- Repo: VideoUse (by Browser Use) lets coding agents perform edits: remove filler words, cut dead space, add subtitles/color/overlays, render, and self-check against transcripts/timestamps.
- Strategy: Start with a single repeatable format (e.g., “founder Loom → 60s launch video,” or “podcast → three clips”), validate quality, then systematize and scale or productize.
- Payoff: Shortens cycle from raw footage to publish-ready assets; converts tacit stylistic rules into agent-readable workflows.

### Treat Skill Installations as a Security Surface
- Risk: Skills/MCP servers integrate code, tools, and behaviors that can access files, services, and instructions—creating prompt injection and data exfiltration exposure.
- Repo: NVIDIA SkillSpecter scans for malicious patterns, supply chain risks, hidden instructions, and MCP-specific issues.
- Usage: Install via UV (e.g., uv tool install git+<repo>), scan local directories or repos (with optional --no-llm for static scans and Docker option to avoid local Python).
- Principle: Pre-install scanning becomes mandatory as agent stacks modularize into a personal “work OS.”

### Put Mobile into the Agent’s Reach
- Gap: Many high-value workflows live only on phones (banking, messaging, social, delivery); APIs are absent or restricted.
- Repo: PhoneHarness connects agents to real iOS/Android devices via macOS iPhone mirroring and ADB—no jailbreak, no special app required.
- Use Cases: Real-device mobile QA (onboarding, signup, checkout), automations for app-only workflows, creator operations across TikTok/Instagram.
- Setup Notes: iOS requires macOS Sequoia with mirroring plus terminal accessibility/screen recording permissions; Android requires Developer Options with ADB (USB or wireless). Verify with phoneharness --doctor.
- Limitation: Human-in-the-loop may be needed for lock screens, Face ID, camera flows; still directionally unlocks a massive tool surface.

## Next Move (Action Items)

**@Content Lead**
- [ ] Draft a 5-post outline set (tweet, LinkedIn, landing page hero, cold email, investor note) and run each through Peter Skill to de-sand while preserving voice; A/B test response rates vs. current baseline - [TBD]

**@RevOps/Founder**
- [ ] Stand up TryComp AI CRM locally (Bun/Docker), configure Google/Microsoft OAuth, and create the “Warm leads I can’t afford to forget” pipeline seeded with 30 recent signals (replies, booked calls, “circle back” mentions) - [TBD]
- [ ] Enable agent-driven follow-ups with a 45/60/90-day cadence and measure reply/conversion lift over 30 days - [TBD]

**@Video Ops**
- [ ] Implement VideoUse for one format: “Podcast → 3 clips” (define subtitle style, pacing, color profile), render a test batch from one episode, and compare edit time and retention vs. manual baseline - [TBD]

**@Security Lead**
- [ ] Integrate NVIDIA SkillSpecter into the skill install pipeline; enforce mandatory scans (with --no-llm for sensitive repos) before any MCP/server/skill is added to the agent stack - [TBD]

**@Mobile QA Lead**
- [ ] Deploy PhoneHarness on a test rig (1 iPhone with macOS Sequoia mirroring, 1 Android via ADB), and script an agent-run mobile signup/checkout QA for the primary app with screenshots and defect notes - [TBD]

recordings.name: 09-02 CRM Automation vs. Sales Workflow: Creating an Exception Status to Prevent Auto-Lost Leads
recordings.summary_md:
## Core Synopsis

A systemic conflict exists between a sales user's workflow and the CRM's automated data hygiene rules. The user, Speaker 1, requires a way to keep leads in an "open" state indefinitely, as their process involves long-term nurturing. However, the system is configured to automatically mark idle leads as "Lost" to prevent data clutter for the broader team. This tension reveals a classic design trade-off: a one-size-fits-all automation that benefits the system's overall health is actively undermining the productivity of a high-performing individual. The immediate need is to find a system-compliant exception or a specific status that exempts designated leads from the automated "Lost" rule.

## The Problem: System Rules vs. User Workflow

### The Pain Point
Speaker 1 is losing visibility on active, long-term leads because the CRM system automatically marks them as "Lost" after a period of inactivity. This automated action directly interferes with their daily task-based follow-up process, forcing them to combat the system instead of using it. The core request is for a state where a lead is never marked "Lost" unless they manually trigger that action.

### The System's Rationale
The automated "Lost" rule is not an error but a deliberate design choice. As explained by Lance, it exists to maintain data hygiene across the entire user base. Without it, the CRM would accumulate thousands of unmanaged, "dead garbage" leads, as most users do not proactively clean their pipelines. The rule serves the collective by preventing data bloat at the expense of individual edge cases.

### The Proposed Workaround
Lance identifies a potential solution within the existing system. There should be a specific lead status, such as "On Order," that is exempt from the automatic "Lost" rule. Placing a lead in this status would allow it to remain in the system indefinitely, effectively creating the exception Speaker 1 needs without requiring a fundamental change to the system-wide rule.

## Next Move

**@Lance**
- [ ] Call the vendor (Gage) to confirm which lead status exempts a lead from being automatically marked "Lost" - [TBD]

recordings.name: 09-02 Auto Dealership's Customer Re-engagement Stalled by Podium Platform Misuse
recordings.summary_md:
![PLAUD NOTE](permanent/1440a4fbcf984caa9625e6345e38a215/mem_g5kZLYofe1/summary_poster/card_20260902154325-v2@cde26a49d69fcaf9ff0328_20260902154413_537a7f21.png)

## Core Synopsis

The dealership's customer re-engagement operation is functionally stalled because the team lacks the basic ability to extract a targeted contact list from its own messaging platform. Speaker 2 sent a "Been a While" loyalty template to an estimated 200–300 former Audi customers — largely legacy accounts from a salesperson named Ryan — and now needs to personally reach out to that specific cohort via personal cell phone as the dealership phases out of a product line. The operational blocker is not the outreach itself, but the inability to filter Podium's inbox to surface that precise recipient list. Compounding this, the conversation exposed a deeper systemic failure: Podium messages are being buried without resolution — a customer had been waiting three weeks for a reply — because the team has not adopted the platform's filtering and task tools with any discipline. Lance pointed to the "Engaged" filter and the task list as the correct triage mechanisms, but the team is clearly not using either consistently. We are sitting on a communication infrastructure that nobody has actually learned to operate, and customers are falling through the gaps because of it.

---

## The Podium Competency Gap: Buried Leads and a Broken Retrieval Workflow

### 1. The Immediate Operational Need

Speaker 2 requires a filtered export of all contacts who received the **"Been a While"** template message — an estimated 200–300 recipients, predominantly former Audi owners previously handled by Ryan. The intent is to transition outreach to personal cell phone contact as the dealership exits a specific product or service line. The Podium platform holds this data, but neither Speaker 2 nor Lance immediately knew the precise export or filter path to retrieve it during the conversation.

### 2. The Systemic Inbox Problem

The conversation surfaced a structural failure in how Podium is being used as a daily triage tool:

- **Messages are going unanswered for weeks.** Speaker 2 cited a customer who waited three weeks for a reply — a direct consequence of replies being buried beneath high-volume outbound blast threads.
- **The "Engaged" filter is the correct tool but unused.** Lance identified the **Engaged** filter as the mechanism to surface contacts who have replied and are awaiting a response. This was apparently unknown or underutilized by the primary daily user.
- **The Task List is not being maintained.** Lance referenced the Podium task list as the intended follow-up safety net. Speaker 2's experience contradicts its effectiveness in practice — the three-week lapse suggests tasks are either not being created or not being checked.

### 3. The Opt-In Friction Point

Speaker 2 expressed reluctance to route outreach through Podium due to the opt-in confirmation message it sends to contacts. Lance clarified that the opt-in checkbox can be pre-selected before sending to suppress that prompt, and that recipients would only receive a standard opt-out notice. For a list of established repeat customers, this distinction is operationally significant and removes the stated barrier to using the platform for follow-up.

---

## Action Items

**@Lance**
- [ ] Pull and deliver the full recipient list for the "Been a While" template — names and contact numbers — for Speaker 2's personal outreach campaign - [TBD]

**@Speaker 2**
- [ ] Use the **Engaged** filter in Podium daily to identify and respond to all contacts awaiting a reply - [TBD]
- [ ] When sending outreach via Podium to existing customers, pre-check the opt-in box to suppress the confirmation prompt - [TBD]

recordings.name: 09-02 Misconfigured AI Clock-Stop Policy in VinSolutions Risks Masking Unworked Leads at Audi Baton Rouge
recordings.summary_md:
## Core Synopsis
The clock-stop policy in VinSolutions (VCA) is mis-specified for Audi Baton Rouge’s transition from Podium to Vens AI: automated replies from “Chloe” are stopping the response timer without a visible distinction from human responses, creating false compliance signals and masking unworked leads. The Sales Operations team changed the assistant’s display name to Chloe, confirming intent to keep AI in the loop, but the current configuration blurs accountability between AI and humans and risks management misreading SLA adherence while customers haven’t received a human follow-up. We are responsible for preventing metric gaming and ensuring operational clarity; the system must show when the clock is stopped by AI versus a human, and Podium must be prevented from affecting the clock during the transition to avoid double-stopping or misleading timestamps.

## VCA Configuration Gap and Transition Risks

### The Operational Gap: AI vs. Human Response Distinction
- Phenomenon: Automated VCA (Chloe) responses can stop the lead response clock in VinSolutions.
- Mechanism: Current settings treat AI replies as equivalent to human responses for SLA timing.
- Consequence: Management dashboards may show timely responses while no human has engaged, risking customer experience and accountability drift.

### Transition Complexity: Podium Deactivation and Overlap Control
- Status: Team is moving off Podium to Vens AI; residual Podium behavior may still stop clocks.
- Risk: Dual systems could both stop or manipulate clock states, compounding tracking errors and obscuring true response ownership during the cutover.

### Governance Requirement: Visibility and Accountability
- Need: A clear indicator in VinSolutions that differentiates “Clock stopped by Chloe (AI)” versus “Clock stopped by Human,” plus a field or flag that shows “Awaiting human follow-up.”
- Stakeholder: Gage (new VinSolutions owner) is the control point to validate configuration options, field labels, and workflow automation to preserve SLA integrity.

## Next Move (Action Items)

**@Gage (VinSolutions Owner)**
- [ ] Audit current VCA settings to identify whether AI (Chloe) replies are configured to stop the response clock and how they are labeled in VinSolutions - [TBD]
- [ ] Implement a visible distinction in VinSolutions between AI-stopped and human-stopped clocks (e.g., custom activity type, status flag, or tag “AI Auto-Reply”) - [TBD]
- [ ] Configure workflow so AI responses do not mark leads as “responded by agent” and add a required “Awaiting human response” flag until a human logs contact - [TBD]
- [ ] Validate reporting fields and dashboards to surface leads where only Chloe responded and escalate any that exceed human-response SLA - [TBD]

**@Lance**
- [ ] Schedule and run a 30-minute configuration review with Gage to confirm the clock-stop logic, labels, and reporting outputs in VinSolutions - [TBD]
- [ ] Define the operational rule: when AI may stop the clock and the maximum window for human follow-up before escalation; document and circulate to Sales Management - [TBD]

**@Podium Administrator**
- [ ] Confirm and enforce that Podium no longer stops or modifies response clocks for Audi Baton Rouge leads; document the exact deactivation steps performed - [TBD]
- [ ] Verify no residual automations or webhooks from Podium are writing to VinSolutions lead timelines; provide verification logs/screenshots - [TBD]

recordings.name: 09-01 Analysis of Marketing Performance and Strategic Realignment
recordings.summary_md:
![PLAUD NOTE](permanent/1440a4fbcf984caa9625e6345e38a215/mem_g5kZLYofe1/summary_poster/card_20260901224331-v2@944f6099177a7543a34eac_20260901224445_b046db58.png)

This conversation documents the termination of Lance's marketing contract due to performance issues, primarily concerning social media and inventory photography. The discussion transitions to a strategic analysis of the dealership's marketing needs, a demonstration of an advanced analytics tool developed by Lance, and the negotiation of a new, consulting-based role for him, culminating in a handover plan for his replacement, Thomas.
------------
## Preliminary Marketing Discussions

The dialogue begins with several operational inquiries before shifting to the main topic of performance. Speaker 2 asks Lance to identify the supplier for previously successful LSU and Southern-themed shirts, which featured "Tigers" and "Jaguars" on the back, with the intent to reorder them. The conversation then turns to an email regarding marketing strategy, where Lance clarifies that while keywords and minor campaigns are running, there is no significant extra spend allocated. He mentions that his Jackson store spends approximately $2,200 on a service marketing program called "Service Combat" but questions if this store needs to invest the full $2,200-$3,000. Speaker 3 interjects, stating the client is interested in buying more keywords and social media services, leading to a brief discussion about Porsche service clinics, for which Lance notes that historical data is available.
------------
## Performance Review and Termination of Contract

The conversation takes a critical turn as Speaker 3 directly informs Lance that a new employee, Thomas, has been hired to replace him. Speaker 3 outlines the reasons for this decision, stating that Lance appears "stretched too thin" across too many accounts, leading to neglect of key priorities. The specific areas of underperformance cited include inconsistent inventory photography and poor social media content, which is characterized as having "zero engagement" and appearing to be just one photo cropped multiple times. Lance defends his photography, explaining his process involves shooting "wides, mediums, and tights" rather than cropping, and that his primary focus has been on higher-level SEO, SEM, and CRM cleanup. Despite his defense, Lance accepts the feedback and the termination, acknowledging that the store's needs for a constant, on-site presence—a "daily guy"—are not aligned with his consulting-focused specialty.
------------
## Transition Planning and Negotiation of a New Role

Following the decision to terminate the current contract, the discussion shifts to organizing a professional transition. Lance agrees to a one-month notice period, during which he will submit one final bill and ensure a complete and smooth handover of responsibilities to his replacement, Thomas. He commits to personally guiding Thomas through all account logins and operational processes. Simultaneously, Lance proposes a new, restructured relationship where he would serve in a high-level consulting capacity, focusing on strategic oversight, data analysis, and managing SEO/SEM vendors, rather than daily content creation. Speaker 3 is receptive to this idea, and they agree to determine an appropriate fee for this new arrangement. A key condition is established: Thomas will be prohibited from working for any competing Porsche dealerships, a term Lance agrees is standard.
------------
## Demonstration of Advanced Marketing Analytics Tool

To underscore his value as a high-level strategist, Lance presents a custom analytics dashboard he developed. He explains that the tool integrates disparate data sources—including website traffic from GA4, CRM lead data from systems like VinSolutions, and live inventory data—into a single, coherent view. He demonstrates its capabilities, showing how it visualizes traffic sources, inventory aging, new/used/CPO splits, and demand shape by model. A key feature highlighted is its ability to de-duplicate lead sources, providing a true picture of retail opportunities by filtering out low-quality leads from buying centers like KBB. Lance uses examples from other dealerships to show how the dashboard can reveal trade-in patterns, sales performance by zip code, and critical operational metrics like lead response times, positioning the tool as a way to be a "guardian of spend" by focusing on improving closing ratios before increasing marketing budgets.
------------
## Strategic Discussion on Dealership Marketing and Operations

The analytics demonstration sparks a broader strategic conversation about the nuances of automotive marketing. The speakers contrast the high-intensity, campaign-driven needs of brands like BMW and Audi with the more brand-insulated market of Porsche, which doesn't require the same level of aggressive marketing overhauls. They discuss the significant, often underestimated, time and expense required for quality content creation, noting a short video can take days to produce. The conversation also touches on operational efficiencies, such as the high cost ($120,000) and effectiveness of "light box" photo booths for consistent vehicle imaging and automated service-lane inspection systems that can significantly raise the hours per repair order (RO) by instantly identifying service needs. They conclude that in a market with product pipeline challenges, like the upcoming shift of the gas-powered Macan to a new model, having a strong service operation and skilled advisors is paramount.
------------
## Action Items

**@Lance**

recordings.name: Review: AMP 2.0 Account Performance and Fullpath Platform Migration
recordings.summary_md:
## AMP 2.0 review + Fullpath / Dealer.com group site

Katie (AMP; Katie Westerfield on the BHBMW brief) and Olivia (Dealer.com) reviewed Brian Harris BMW / group AMP 2.0 with Lance. No spoken dest. No Ada work order.

**Dealer.com group site (brianharrisautogroup.com).** Olivia dropped in to check on the neglected group site. She will email draft links, optimization notes, and a homepage demo page. Review stays on the existing recurring AMP call **September 22, 2026** — Katie will add Olivia to that series. Store website vendor on the brief remains Motive; this is the group Dealer.com property.

**Mileage / Your Garage.** A customer (routed via Thomas/Elizabeth shared email → Brett) flagged a trade-in mileage estimate as way off. Logic: last service odometer + **1,000 miles/month**. Last visit was 2020 at ~57–58k, so six years of add-on blew the number for a low-mileage driver. Decision: exclude customers whose last service visit was **over three years ago**. Katie will change the campaign rule.

**Fullpath.** Cox bought Fullpath and is moving AMP clients over. Existing AMP pricing is grandfathered (direct Fullpath would be a different tier). Optional add-ons get a **60-day free trial**, then paid. AMP stays live at least another month even if they demo immediately. No Fullpath rep has emailed Lance. Katie will introduce Lance **and Brett** today and send a calendar link.

**AMP 2.0 dashboard (spoken).** 39% engagement. Email-first because the account is on a dedicated new domain (better email response; fewer auto texts than AMP 1.0 — ad-hoc texts are on Lance/Katie). 306 tasks created. 15 AMP-attributed sales (5 pre-owned); one delivered unit missing CRM price match. Example: Monet Ford got Your Garage Jul 28, bought a 2026 X1 Aug 14. 14 direct leads, 77 indirect, 296 repair orders, revenue ~$230k. Katie will do a text-heavy Labor Day ad-hoc (skip design) and doctor the X3/X5/X7 email from the live offer link Lance dropped in chat (verbiage, fine print, Consumer Reports SUV blurb).

**CRM housekeeping (Lance).** Service customers with no assigned sales rep are landing unassigned (~20+ on page two). Filter lead status **active / sold / lost**. Tristan still has ~1,100 tasks and is gone. Jason is still at the store but not on this work. Katie: set a **round-robin** so new service-originated AMP tasks auto-distribute. Opportunity list is on by default in 2.0 and doubled with tasks — Katie prefers tasks for accountability.

**Dest:** dealers / bhbmw (inferred — AMP + BHBMW / Harris BMW service + group site; no spoken dest).
**Disposition:** park — file only. Katie/Olivia own vendor follow-ups. Lance owns CRM reassignment. No “build this” / Todoist / email / meeting-setup ask for Ada.
**Vendor-brief path:** taken — GM meeting notes + BHBMW brief row.
